# AGENT_GUIDELINES.md

**Audience:** Every contributor to this codebase — human or AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, etc.)
**Purpose:** One source of truth for architecture, style, and workflow so that code generated by any contributor is indistinguishable in quality and shape from code written by any other contributor.

If a rule in this document conflicts with a rule you'd normally follow, **this document wins** for this repository.

## 1. Project Philosophy

This project follows a **pragmatic Clean Architecture** — layered enough to keep business logic testable and UI dumb, but not so layered that adding a text field requires touching six files. When a rule below says "always," it means always; when it says "prefer," a documented exception is fine as long as it's called out in the PR description.

Core principles, in priority order:

1. **Predictability over cleverness.** Any contributor (or agent) should be able to guess where a piece of code lives before searching for it.
2. **Feature-first, layer-second.** Features are the unit of ownership; layers are the unit of organization inside a feature.
3. **Widgets are dumb. Cubits are smart. Repositories are the only ones who know about the network.** No layer skips another.
4. **One way to do a thing.** If two patterns solve the same problem, we pick one and delete the other. AI agents must not introduce a second pattern "because it's also valid."
5. **Consistency beats micro-optimization.** A slightly less "clever" widget that matches the rest of the codebase is more valuable than a uniquely optimized one.
6. **Testability is a design constraint, not an afterthought.** Even before tests are written, code must be *shaped* so tests are trivial to add later (see [Section 15](#15-testing-expectations)).
7. **No dead code, no placeholders, no `TODO: implement later` in generated output.** If something can't be finished, it must be flagged in the PR description, not silently stubbed.

## 2. Architecture

We use a 6-layer model per feature. Every feature module is a vertical slice through these layers.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        PRESENTATION                          │
│   Widgets, Pages, Screens — pure UI, no logic                │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ listens to / dispatches events
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                     STATE MANAGEMENT                          │
│   Cubit + State (freezed) — orchestrates use cases,           │
│   holds UI state, converts domain results into view state    │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ calls
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                          DOMAIN                               │
│   Entities + (optional) UseCases — pure Dart, no Flutter,      │
│   no Dio, no GetIt. Business rules live here.                  │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ calls interface
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                        REPOSITORY                              │
│   Interface + Impl — translates between Domain and Data,       │
│   decides caching/offline strategy, converts exceptions         │
│   into typed Failures                                          │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ calls
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                       DATA SOURCE                              │
│   Remote / Local data sources — knows about DTOs, raw           │
│   JSON, SharedPreferences, Hive, etc.                           │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                            │ calls
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                            API                                 │
│   Dio client, interceptors, base URLs, headers                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Layer contracts (CAN / CANNOT)

| Layer | CAN access | CANNOT access |
|---|---|---|
| **Presentation** (widgets, pages) | Cubit (via `context.read`/`BlocBuilder`), other widgets, theme, router | Repository, Data Source, Dio, `GetIt` directly, domain entities' business methods, SharedPreferences |
| **State Management** (Cubit) | Domain entities, Repository *interfaces* (injected), other Cubits' public state (read-only, rare) | Widgets, `BuildContext` (except passed-in navigation callbacks resolved in the widget layer — see [§7](#7-business-logic)), Dio, DTOs, Data Sources directly |
| **Domain** (entities, use cases) | Only pure Dart, other domain entities | Flutter SDK, Repository implementations, Dio, DTOs, `GetIt`, Cubits |
| **Repository** (interface + impl) | Data Sources, domain entities, DTO→Entity mappers | Widgets, Cubits, `BuildContext` |
| **Data Source** | Dio/API client, DTOs, local storage APIs | Domain entities directly (it deals in DTOs), Cubits, widgets |
| **API** (Dio client) | HTTP concerns only: headers, interceptors, base config | Business logic, DTOs' business meaning, feature-specific code |

**Golden rule:** a layer may only talk to the layer directly beneath it. A Cubit never imports `dio`. A widget never imports a repository. A Data Source never imports `flutter_bloc`.

## 3. Folder Structure

Feature-first at the top, layered inside each feature. This mirrors and formalizes the existing `lib/<feature>/` pattern (`login/`, `role_selection/`, `caregiver/`, `splash/`, `welcome_screen/`).

```
lib/
├── main_development.dart
├── main_staging.dart
├── main_production.dart
├── bootstrap.dart
│
├── app/
│   ├── app.dart                       # barrel
│   ├── view/
│   │   └── app.dart                   # MaterialApp.router, theming, locale
│   └── routes/
│       ├── app_router.dart            # GoRouter config
│       └── app_routes.dart            # route path/name constants
│
├── core/                              # shared, feature-agnostic code only
│   ├── constants/
│   │   ├── app_constants.dart
│   │   ├── api_constants.dart
│   │   └── storage_keys.dart
│   ├── network/
│   │   ├── api_client.dart            # Dio wrapper
│   │   ├── api_response.dart
│   │   └── interceptors/
│   │       ├── auth_interceptor.dart
│   │       └── logging_interceptor.dart
│   ├── error/
│   │   ├── failure.dart               # freezed sealed Failure types
│   │   └── exceptions.dart            # thrown by data sources
│   ├── di/
│   │   ├── injection.dart             # GetIt + injectable setup
│   │   └── injection.config.dart      # generated
│   ├── theme/
│   │   └── app_theme.dart
│   ├── utils/
│   │   ├── validators.dart
│   │   └── formatters.dart
│   └── widgets/                       # TRULY generic, cross-feature widgets only
│       ├── app_button.dart
│       ├── app_text_field.dart
│       ├── loading_indicator.dart
│       └── error_view.dart
│
├── <feature_name>/                    # e.g. caregiver/
│   ├── <feature_name>.dart            # barrel export
│   ├── data/
│   │   ├── datasources/
│   │   │   ├── <feature>_remote_data_source.dart
│   │   │   └── <feature>_local_data_source.dart
│   │   ├── models/                    # DTOs (freezed + json_serializable)
│   │   │   └── <thing>_dto.dart
│   │   └── repositories/
│   │       └── <feature>_repository_impl.dart
│   ├── domain/
│   │   ├── entities/
│   │   │   └── <thing>.dart           # freezed, no JSON annotations
│   │   └── repositories/
│   │       └── <feature>_repository.dart   # abstract interface
│   ├── cubit/
│   │   ├── <feature>_cubit.dart
│   │   └── <feature>_state.dart       # freezed
│   ├── view/
│   │   └── <feature>_page.dart        # top-level screen, wires up Cubit
│   └── widgets/
│       └── <feature>_card.dart        # feature-local, reusable within feature only
│
└── l10n/
    ├── l10n.dart
    ├── arb/
    │   ├── app_en.arb
    │   └── app_bn.arb
    └── gen/
        └── app_localizations.dart
```

### What belongs where

- **`data/datasources/`** — talks to Dio or local storage, returns/consumes **DTOs**, throws typed `Exception`s (never returns `null` silently, never swallows errors).
- **`data/models/`** — DTOs only. Annotated with `@freezed` + `@JsonSerializable`. Contain `fromJson`/`toJson` and a `toEntity()` mapper. No business logic beyond mapping.
- **`data/repositories/`** — implements the domain interface, calls data sources, converts thrown `Exception`s into `Failure`s, maps DTOs → Entities.
- **`domain/entities/`** — `@freezed` classes with no JSON annotations, no Flutter imports. May contain simple derived getters (e.g. `bool get isEligible`) if it's a pure business rule.
- **`domain/repositories/`** — abstract classes only. This is the contract the Cubit depends on (dependency inversion).
- **`cubit/`** — one Cubit + one State per feature slice (a feature can have more than one Cubit if it has more than one independent piece of state — e.g. `CaregiverListCubit` vs `CaregiverFilterCubit`).
- **`view/`** — one page/screen per file, wraps content in a `BlocProvider` (using `getIt<Cubit>()`), delegates all rendering to widgets.
- **`widgets/` (feature-local)** — widgets only used within this feature. If a widget is needed by two or more features, promote it to `core/widgets/`.

A file never contains more than one public top-level class, with the exception of a small private helper widget used only by that file (see [§13](#13-widget-guidelines)).

## 4. State Management Rules

### When to use a Cubit (vs. Bloc)

**Default to Cubit.** Use `Bloc` (event-based) only when a feature genuinely needs to react to overlapping/queued async events (e.g. a stream of WebSocket real-time updates needs debouncing/queuing logic) — most CRUD/screen state does not need this. If in doubt, start with Cubit; escalate to Bloc only when Cubit's direct-method-call model becomes awkward.

### What belongs inside a Cubit

- Calling repository methods and awaiting results.
- Converting `Either<Failure, T>` (or try/catch) results into `State` variants (`loading`, `loaded`, `error`).
- Simple, UI-agnostic transformations of data for display (e.g. sorting a list the Cubit fetched) — **not** formatting for display (that's the widget's job, see [§7](#7-business-logic)).
- Debouncing/search-as-you-type logic, pagination cursors, form field validity aggregation.
- Emitting one state per logical change. Never emit "in-between" partial states that a widget has to guess about.

```dart
@injectable
class CaregiverListCubit extends Cubit<CaregiverListState> {
  CaregiverListCubit(this._repository) : super(const CaregiverListState.initial());

  final CaregiverRepository _repository;

  Future<void> fetchCaregivers() async {
    emit(const CaregiverListState.loading());
    final result = await _repository.getCaregivers();
    result.when(
      success: (caregivers) => emit(CaregiverListState.loaded(caregivers)),
      failure: (failure) => emit(CaregiverListState.error(failure.message)),
    );
  }
}
```

### What should NEVER go inside widgets

- Direct repository or data source calls.
- `Dio` instances or HTTP status code checks.
- Business rules (e.g. "a caregiver is only bookable if rating > 3.5 and verified").
- Manual `try/catch` around async business operations — that belongs in the Cubit/Repository.
- Mutable fields that represent business state (a `StatefulWidget`'s `State` may hold **purely visual** state — an animation controller, a scroll controller, a text field's focus — never business data that outlives the widget's lifecycle).
- Direct `GetIt.instance<T>()` calls scattered through widget trees — resolve dependencies once, at the `BlocProvider` / page level.

## 5. UI Guidelines

### Component-based UI

Every screen is composed of small, named widgets — never one large `build()` method with inline anonymous widget trees. A widget is "a component" if it has a name, a single visual responsibility, and could plausibly be reused or tested in isolation.

### When to extract a widget

Extract when **any** of these is true:
- The widget subtree is used in more than one place → always extract to `core/widgets/` or feature `widgets/`.
- A single logical block inside `build()` exceeds ~20 lines → extract, even if used once, to keep `build()` readable.
- The subtree has its own local visual state (e.g. an expandable card) → extract as its own `StatefulWidget`.
- You're tempted to add a comment like `// --- Header section ---` inside `build()` → that comment is a widget name in disguise. Extract it.

### Widget composition

Prefer composition (passing widgets as parameters/children) over configuration (a widget with 15 boolean flags). If a widget needs many optional visual variants, split it into two purpose-named widgets rather than one widget with a `bool isCompact` flag fanning out internal `if`s.

### Reusable widgets

Before creating a new widget, **search `core/widgets/` and the current feature's `widgets/` folder.** A near-duplicate widget is a bug, not a convenience. If an existing widget is *almost* right, extend it with a new named constructor or optional parameter rather than copy-pasting.

### Design consistency

All spacing, colors, and text styles come from `AppTheme` / `Theme.of(context)`. Raw hex colors, raw `EdgeInsets` numbers, and raw `TextStyle`s in feature code are a code-review blocker.

**Bad:**
```dart
Container(
  padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
  color: const Color(0xFF2E7D32),
  child: Text('Book now', style: TextStyle(fontSize: 16, color: Colors.white)),
)
```

**Good:**
```dart
Container(
  padding: EdgeInsets.all(AppSpacing.md),
  color: theme.colorScheme.primary,
  child: Text('Book now', style: theme.textTheme.titleMedium),
)
```

---

## 6. Build Method Rules

A clean `build()` method:

- Returns a **shallow** tree: at most 3–4 levels of nesting before delegating to a named widget.
- Contains **no business logic** — only `if`/ternary for purely visual branching (e.g. `state.isLoading ? const LoadingIndicator() : CaregiverList(...)`).
- Reads state via `BlocBuilder`/`BlocSelector` at the narrowest possible scope — wrap only the subtree that needs to rebuild, not the whole page.
- Has no inline anonymous functions longer than a single expression — extract to a named method or a `Cubit` method.

**Avoiding deep nesting:**
- Extract every `Column`/`Row` child group of 3+ widgets into its own widget.
- Prefer early return / guard clauses at the top of `build()` for loading/error/empty states instead of nesting the "happy path" three levels deep inside conditionals.

```dart
@override
Widget build(BuildContext context) {
  return BlocBuilder<CaregiverListCubit, CaregiverListState>(
    builder: (context, state) {
      return state.when(
        initial: () => const SizedBox.shrink(),
        loading: () => const LoadingIndicator(),
        error: (message) => ErrorView(message: message),
        loaded: (caregivers) => CaregiverListView(caregivers: caregivers),
      );
    },
  );
}
```

## 7. Business Logic

| Concern | Belongs in |
|---|---|
| Input validation (email format, required fields) | `core/utils/validators.dart` (pure functions), invoked from the Cubit on field-change events |
| Business rule validation (e.g. "booking requires verified caregiver") | Domain entity getter or a small use-case function, called from the Cubit |
| API calls | Data Source only, via Repository |
| Navigation (deciding *where* to go) | Cubit emits a state or a one-off signal (e.g. `state.status == FormStatus.success`); the **widget** listens via `BlocListener` and calls `context.go(...)` / `context.push(...)`. Cubits never hold a `BuildContext` or call `go_router` directly. |
| Formatting for display (dates, currency, distance) | `core/utils/formatters.dart`, called from the **widget** at render time — not stored pre-formatted in state |

```dart
// Cubit: decides *that* navigation should happen, not *how*
BlocListener<LoginCubit, LoginState>(
  listener: (context, state) {
    if (state.status == FormStatus.success) {
      context.go(AppRoutes.roleSelection);
    }
  },
  child: ...,
)
```

## 8. Networking

### Repository pattern

The Repository is the single seam between Domain/Cubit and the outside world. It:
1. Calls one or more data sources.
2. Catches `Exception`s thrown by data sources.
3. Maps them into typed `Failure`s (see [§10](#10-error-handling)).
4. Maps returned DTOs into domain Entities before returning.

Cubits depend on the **abstract** repository interface (`domain/repositories/`), never the concrete impl — this keeps Cubits testable with a mock.

### Dio usage

- One shared `Dio` instance, configured in `core/network/api_client.dart`, injected via `GetIt`/`injectable`.
- All interceptors (auth token attachment, logging, error normalization) live in `core/network/interceptors/`.
- Feature data sources receive the shared `ApiClient` — they never instantiate their own `Dio`.
- Data sources throw typed exceptions (`ServerException`, `NetworkException`, `UnauthorizedException`) — never let a raw `DioException` escape past the data source layer.

```dart
@injectable
class CaregiverRemoteDataSource {
  CaregiverRemoteDataSource(this._client);
  final ApiClient _client;

  Future<List<CaregiverDto>> getCaregivers() async {
    try {
      final response = await _client.get(ApiConstants.caregivers);
      return (response.data as List)
          .map((json) => CaregiverDto.fromJson(json))
          .toList();
    } on DioException catch (e) {
      throw ServerException.fromDioException(e);
    }
  }
}
```

### DTOs vs Entities

- **DTO** (`data/models/`): mirrors the API's JSON shape exactly. Has `fromJson`/`toJson`. May contain nullable fields the API sends inconsistently. Never used past the Repository boundary.
- **Entity** (`domain/entities/`): the app's internal business shape. Non-nullable where the business logic requires a value. No JSON annotations. This is what Cubits, widgets, and business rules operate on.
- The DTO has a `toEntity()` method; the Repository is the only place that calls it.

---

## 9. Dependency Injection

- `GetIt` is the service locator; `injectable` generates the registration code — **never** hand-write `getIt.registerSingleton(...)` calls except in `core/di/injection.dart`'s manual module overrides (e.g. registering the `Dio` instance itself, or environment-specific config).
- Annotate classes with `@injectable` (factory — new instance per resolution; used for Cubits) or `@lazySingleton` (one instance for the app's lifetime; used for Repositories, Data Sources, `ApiClient`).
- Abstract repository → concrete impl bindings use `@Injectable(as: CaregiverRepository)` on the impl class.
- Run `flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` after any DI-annotated class changes; commit the regenerated `injection.config.dart`.
- Widgets resolve a Cubit via `getIt<T>()` **only** at the point of constructing a `BlocProvider` in a `view/` page — never inside a deeply nested widget.

```dart
BlocProvider(
  create: (_) => getIt<CaregiverListCubit>()..fetchCaregivers(),
  child: const CaregiverListView(),
)
```

---

## 10. Error Handling

Errors flow in one direction and change shape exactly once per layer:

```
Dio throws DioException
        ↓ (Data Source catches, rethrows as typed Exception)
ServerException / NetworkException / CacheException
        ↓ (Repository catches, maps to Failure)
Failure (freezed sealed class: server, network, cache, unexpected)
        ↓ (Cubit catches, maps to state)
State.error(userFacingMessage)
        ↓ (Widget renders)
ErrorView / SnackBar
```

- **Exceptions** are thrown between Data Source → Repository only; they're an implementation detail of "how the failure happened."
- **Failures** are the business-level, typed representation the rest of the app reasons about (`Failure.server`, `Failure.network`, `Failure.unauthorized`, `Failure.unexpected`).
- **User-facing messages** are decided at the Cubit or widget level, mapped from `Failure` type — never surface a raw exception message or stack trace to the UI.

```dart
@freezed
class Failure with _$Failure {
  const factory Failure.server(String message) = ServerFailure;
  const factory Failure.network() = NetworkFailure;
  const factory Failure.unauthorized() = UnauthorizedFailure;
  const factory Failure.unexpected() = UnexpectedFailure;
}
```

Never use a bare `catch (e) {}` that swallows the error silently. Every catch block either rethrows a typed exception/failure or logs + emits an error state.

## 11. Models

- **DTOs** live in `data/models/`, annotated `@freezed` + `@JsonSerializable(explicitToJson: true)`. Generated via `build_runner`. Always include a `toEntity()` mapper method.
- **Entities** live in `domain/entities/`, annotated `@freezed` only (no JSON codegen needed since they never (de)serialize directly).
- Use `freezed`'s union types for anything with multiple mutually-exclusive shapes (states, failures, sealed API responses) instead of a single class with nullable fields and a `type` enum.
- Run codegen with:
  ```bash
  flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
  ```
  after any change to a `@freezed`/`@JsonSerializable`/`@injectable` class. Generated `.freezed.dart`/`.g.dart`/`.config.dart` files are committed to the repo (not gitignored) so CI and other contributors don't need to regenerate them to build.

```dart
@freezed
class CaregiverDto with _$CaregiverDto {
  const CaregiverDto._();

  const factory CaregiverDto({
    required String id,
    required String name,
    double? rating,
    @Default(false) bool isVerified,
  }) = _CaregiverDto;

  factory CaregiverDto.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) =>
      _$CaregiverDtoFromJson(json);

  Caregiver toEntity() => Caregiver(
        id: id,
        name: name,
        rating: rating ?? 0.0,
        isVerified: isVerified,
      );
}
```

## 12. Naming Conventions

| Item | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Files | `snake_case.dart` | `caregiver_list_cubit.dart` |
| Folders | `snake_case` | `role_selection/` |
| Widgets (classes) | `PascalCase`, noun-first | `CaregiverCard`, `AppButton` |
| Pages/Screens | `PascalCase` + `Page` suffix | `CaregiverListPage` |
| Cubits | `PascalCase` + `Cubit` suffix | `CaregiverListCubit` |
| States | `PascalCase` + `State` suffix; freezed union members as verbs/adjectives | `CaregiverListState`, `.loading()`, `.loaded()`, `.error()` |
| Repositories (interface) | `PascalCase` + `Repository` | `CaregiverRepository` |
| Repositories (impl) | `PascalCase` + `RepositoryImpl` | `CaregiverRepositoryImpl` |
| Data Sources | `PascalCase` + `RemoteDataSource`/`LocalDataSource` | `CaregiverRemoteDataSource` |
| DTOs | `PascalCase` + `Dto` | `CaregiverDto` |
| Entities | `PascalCase`, no suffix | `Caregiver` |
| Enums | `PascalCase` name, `camelCase` values | `enum BookingStatus { pending, confirmed, cancelled }` |
| Extensions | `PascalCase` + `Extension` suffix, named by the type extended | `DateTimeExtension`, `StringExtension` |
| Constants | `camelCase` inside a class holding `static const` (no global loose `const`s) | `AppConstants.maxNameLength` |
| Booleans | prefixed `is`/`has`/`can`/`should` | `isVerified`, `hasError`, `canBook` |

## 13. Widget Guidelines

### Stateless vs Stateful

Default to `StatelessWidget`. Use `StatefulWidget` only when the widget owns transient, purely visual state that a Cubit shouldn't manage: `TextEditingController`, `ScrollController`, `AnimationController`, local expand/collapse UI toggles with no business meaning.

### Preferred widget size

A widget file should rarely exceed ~150 lines including imports. If it's growing past that, its `build()` method is doing too much — extract sub-widgets.

### When to split widgets

See [§5](#5-ui-guidelines) extraction rules. Additionally: split whenever a widget takes more than ~6 constructor parameters — that's usually a sign it should be decomposed into a parent that composes two focused children.

### Custom widgets

Every custom widget:
- Has a `const` constructor wherever possible.
- Takes explicit, named, typed parameters (no passing a whole `state` object into a leaf widget "just in case" — pass only the fields it needs).
- Lives in `core/widgets/` if cross-feature, otherwise in the feature's `widgets/`.

### Common reusable widgets (already expected in `core/widgets/`)

`AppButton`, `AppTextField`, `LoadingIndicator`, `ErrorView`, `EmptyStateView`, `AppCard`, `AppAvatar`. Check this list — and the folder itself — before creating a new generic widget.

---

## 14. Code Style

- **Function length:** aim for ≤ 30 lines. A longer function is a signal to extract a helper.
- **Class size:** aim for ≤ 200 lines. Cubits that grow past this usually need to be split by responsibility (e.g. separate `CaregiverListCubit` and `CaregiverFilterCubit`).
- **Comments:** explain *why*, not *what*. Delete comments that just restate the code. Public classes/methods on Repositories and Cubits get a one-line `///` doc comment describing intent.
- **Variable naming:** full words, no abbreviations (`caregiver`, not `cg`). Loop indices (`i`, `j`) are fine only in tight numeric loops.
- **Constants:** no magic numbers/strings in feature code. Extract to `AppConstants`/`ApiConstants` or a local `static const` at the top of the file if it's file-scoped only.
- **Early returns:** guard clauses at the top of a function instead of nested `if`s.
- **Null safety:** avoid `!` (bang) outside of tests and truly-guaranteed-non-null contexts (e.g. right after a null check). Prefer `?.`, `??`, and exhaustive pattern matching on freezed unions.
- **Immutability:** all models are immutable (`freezed`); no mutable public fields on entities/DTOs/state classes.
- **`const` constructors:** use `const` everywhere the compiler allows it — this is a lint error (`prefer_const_constructors`), not a style suggestion.
- **Trailing commas:** always include, so `dart format` produces stable, readable multi-line diffs.
- **Linter:** `very_good_analysis` as the base rule set (already a dev dependency); no rule is disabled in code with an inline `// ignore:` without a comment explaining why, reviewed in the PR.

---

## 15. Testing Expectations

Even before a formal test suite exists, code must be **structured for testability**:

- Cubits depend on **abstract** repository interfaces (never concrete impls) so a `MockCaregiverRepository` (via `mocktail`) can be substituted in tests without touching real Dio/network code.
- Widgets take data via constructor parameters rather than reaching into `GetIt` themselves — this lets a widget be pumped in a `WidgetTester` with fake data and no DI setup.
- Pure functions (`validators.dart`, `formatters.dart`) contain zero Flutter/Cubit dependencies, so they're unit-testable with plain `test()` blocks.
- Every Cubit's public method should be a deterministic function of (current state + repository result) → new state, so `bloc_test`'s `blocTest()` pattern (`build`, `act`, `expect`) can be dropped in directly once tests are written.
- Test file locations mirror `lib/`: `test/<feature>/cubit/<feature>_cubit_test.dart`, `test/core/utils/validators_test.dart`, etc.

---

## 16. Performance Guidelines

- **`const` widgets:** apply `const` aggressively — it's the cheapest rebuild-avoidance available and is enforced by the linter.
- **Rebuild optimization:** scope `BlocBuilder` to the smallest subtree that needs the changed data. Never wrap an entire page in one `BlocBuilder` if only a small badge/counter needs to update.
- **`BlocBuilder` vs `BlocSelector`:** if a widget only needs one field from a larger state object, use `BlocSelector<Cubit, State, FieldType>` so it only rebuilds when that field changes — not on every state emission.
- **Image loading:** use cached network image loading (e.g. `CachedNetworkImage`) for all remote images (caregiver photos, etc.), never a raw `Image.network` without a cache/placeholder/error builder.
- **Lazy loading:** long lists (caregiver search results, chat history) use `ListView.builder`/`SliverList`, never `Column` + `map()` inside a `SingleChildScrollView`.
- **List performance:** provide `key`s on list items when the list can reorder/filter, so Flutter can diff efficiently instead of rebuilding every tile.

---

## 17. AI Agent Instructions

These rules are binding for any AI coding assistant working in this repository:

1. **Search before you create.** Before writing a new widget, util function, or model, search `core/widgets/`, `core/utils/`, and the current feature's folder for something that already does this. Never duplicate existing widgets or helpers.
2. **Follow the existing feature structure exactly.** New features get `data/`, `domain/`, `cubit/`, `view/`, `widgets/` subfolders in the pattern shown in [§3](#3-folder-structure) — do not invent a new structure for "this one feature."
3. **Keep widgets single-responsibility.** If a `build()` method is doing more than one visual job, split it per [§5](#5-ui-guidelines)/[§6](#6-build-method-rules) before finishing the task.
4. **Never place business logic in the UI layer.** Validation, API calls, navigation decisions, and formatting rules belong where [§7](#7-business-logic) says they belong — not inline in a widget.
5. **Reuse the theme and design system.** No raw colors, raw `TextStyle`s, or raw spacing numbers in feature code — use `Theme.of(context)` / `AppTheme` / `AppSpacing`.
6. **Never introduce a new dependency without flagging it.** If a task seems to need a new pub package, stop and call this out explicitly in your response rather than silently adding it to `pubspec.yaml`.
7. **Generate production-ready code only.** No `// TODO: implement`, no stub methods that return hardcoded fake data disguised as real logic, no commented-out alternative implementations left in the file.
8. **Regenerate code after model/DI changes.** Any edit to a `@freezed`, `@JsonSerializable`, or `@injectable` class must be followed by running `build_runner` (or explicitly telling the human to run it) and updating the generated file references.
9. **Match existing naming conventions exactly** — see [§12](#12-naming-conventions). Do not introduce a new naming scheme "for clarity."
10. **Respect layer boundaries strictly** — see the CAN/CANNOT table in [§2](#2-architecture). A generated Cubit that imports `dio` or a generated widget that imports a repository is a bug, not a shortcut.
11. **Prefer editing over rewriting.** When modifying existing code, make the smallest change that satisfies the request; don't reformat or restructure unrelated code in the same file.
12. **State your assumptions.** If a request is ambiguous (e.g. which feature a shared widget belongs in), pick the most consistent option per this document and say so, rather than silently guessing or asking unnecessarily.

---

## 18. Pull Request Checklist

Before code (human- or AI-generated) is considered done:

- [ ] No layer-boundary violations (widget → repository, Cubit → Dio, etc.)
- [ ] No business logic inside `build()` methods or widget classes
- [ ] All new widgets checked against `core/widgets/` and feature `widgets/` for duplicates
- [ ] All colors/spacing/text styles come from the theme, no raw values
- [ ] New/changed `@freezed`/`@JsonSerializable`/`@injectable` classes have regenerated `.freezed.dart`/`.g.dart`/`.config.dart` committed
- [ ] DTOs stay within `data/`; only Entities cross into `domain`/`cubit`/`view`
- [ ] Errors are typed (`Exception` → `Failure` → `State`), no raw exception text shown to users
- [ ] No `print()` statements; use the existing logger/interceptor
- [ ] No magic numbers/strings; extracted to constants
- [ ] `const` used everywhere the compiler allows
- [ ] Trailing commas present on multi-line calls/constructors
- [ ] No new dependency added without explicit approval noted in the PR description
- [ ] No leftover TODOs, commented-out code, or placeholder/mock logic disguised as real implementation
- [ ] Naming follows [§12](#12-naming-conventions) exactly
- [ ] `flutter analyze` and `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` both pass clean

## 19. Examples

### Example A — Fetching and displaying a list

**Bad** (logic in widget, Dio in UI, no layering):
```dart
class CaregiverListPage extends StatefulWidget {
  @override
  State<CaregiverListPage> createState() => _CaregiverListPageState();
}

class _CaregiverListPageState extends State<CaregiverListPage> {
  List<dynamic> caregivers = [];

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    Dio().get('https://api.example.com/caregivers').then((res) {
      setState(() => caregivers = res.data);
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return ListView(
      children: caregivers.map((c) => Container(
        padding: EdgeInsets.all(16),
        color: Color(0xFFEFEFEF),
        child: Column(children: [
          Text(c['name'], style: TextStyle(fontSize: 18)),
          Text('${c['rating']} ★'),
          if (c['isVerified'] == true) Text('Verified', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.green)),
        ]),
      )).toList(),
    );
  }
}
```
*Problems:* raw HTTP in a widget, no error/loading states, raw JSON maps instead of typed models, raw colors/styles, no layer separation, `StatefulWidget` used for business state.

**Better** (proper layering, still simple):
```dart
class CaregiverListPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const CaregiverListPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return BlocProvider(
      create: (_) => getIt<CaregiverListCubit>()..fetchCaregivers(),
      child: const CaregiverListView(),
    );
  }
}

class CaregiverListView extends StatelessWidget {
  const CaregiverListView({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return BlocBuilder<CaregiverListCubit, CaregiverListState>(
      builder: (context, state) => state.when(
        initial: () => const SizedBox.shrink(),
        loading: () => const LoadingIndicator(),
        error: (message) => ErrorView(message: message),
        loaded: (caregivers) => ListView.builder(
          itemCount: caregivers.length,
          itemBuilder: (_, i) => CaregiverCard(caregiver: caregivers[i]),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

**Best practice** (adds `BlocSelector` for a badge that only needs the count, keeps `CaregiverCard` fully decomposed):
```dart
class CaregiverListView extends StatelessWidget {
  const CaregiverListView({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Column(
      children: [
        const _ResultsCountBadge(),
        Expanded(
          child: BlocBuilder<CaregiverListCubit, CaregiverListState>(
            builder: (context, state) => state.when(
              initial: () => const SizedBox.shrink(),
              loading: () => const LoadingIndicator(),
              error: (message) => ErrorView(message: message),
              loaded: (caregivers) => CaregiverListBody(caregivers: caregivers),
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

class _ResultsCountBadge extends StatelessWidget {
  const _ResultsCountBadge();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return BlocSelector<CaregiverListCubit, CaregiverListState, int>(
      selector: (state) => state.maybeWhen(loaded: (list) => list.length, orElse: () => 0),
      builder: (context, count) => Text('$count caregivers found'),
    );
  }
}
```
*Why this is preferred:* the badge rebuilds independently of the list body via `BlocSelector`, the list body is its own named widget (`CaregiverListBody`), and every rule from [§4](#4-state-management-rules)–[§6](#6-build-method-rules) is satisfied.

---

### Example B — Form validation and submission

**Bad:**
```dart
ElevatedButton(
  onPressed: () {
    if (emailController.text.contains('@') && passwordController.text.length >= 6) {
      Dio().post('/login', data: {'email': emailController.text, 'password': passwordController.text})
        .then((res) => Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/home'));
    } else {
      ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(SnackBar(content: Text('Invalid')));
    }
  },
  child: Text('Login'),
)
```

**Better:**
```dart
ElevatedButton(
  onPressed: () => context.read<LoginCubit>().submit(),
  child: const Text('Login'),
)
```
with validation and submission fully inside `LoginCubit`, using `Validators.isValidEmail` from `core/utils/validators.dart`.

**Best practice:** the button is wrapped by a `BlocListener` at the page level that reacts to `state.status == FormStatus.success` to navigate via `go_router`, and a `BlocSelector<LoginCubit, LoginState, bool>` on `state.isValid` controls the button's `onPressed`/disabled look — matching [§7](#7-business-logic) exactly.

---

### Example C — Model definition

**Bad** (mutable, no separation between API shape and business shape):
```dart
class Caregiver {
  String name;
  var rating;
  Map<String, dynamic> raw;
  Caregiver.fromJson(this.raw) {
    name = raw['name'];
    rating = raw['rating'];
  }
}
```

**Better/Best practice:** see the `CaregiverDto` example in [§11](#11-models) — immutable, `freezed`, explicit `toEntity()` mapping, no raw dynamic maps leaking past the data source.
